title: Holy Saturday
hookLine: the quiet day; in the old vigil a new fire is lit in the dark

cards: The day after a funeral has its own kind of quiet. The flowers are still there, the casseroles in the fridge. Everyone has gone home.
The Gospels give this day almost nothing. Jesus has been laid in a new tomb cut in the rock, a great stone rolled to the door.
Luke says the women went home, prepared spices to anoint the body, "and rested the sabbath day according to the commandment." Matthew adds only that a guard is posted and the stone sealed.
Nobody in the story knows what comes next. Today's word is the name of that silence.

teach.h: A DAY OF SILENCE AND WAITING.
teach.b: Holy Saturday. For most of the day, churches stay bare and quiet, no celebration yet: a day for waiting in grief. But Christians have also wondered where Jesus was that day.
The Apostles' Creed says, in the Book of Common Prayer, "He descended into hell." The First Letter of Peter says he "went and preached unto the spirits in prison."

Out of those lines grew an old picture, sometimes called the harrowing of hell. In the Orthodox Easter icon, Christ stands on the broken gates of death, pulling Adam and Eve up out of their tombs by the wrists.
Christians read that line of the creed in more than one way: some as a descent to the dead, some as a way of saying he truly died. Then night falls, and something happens in the dark.

teach.h: A NEW FIRE IN THE DARK.
teach.b: In the old Easter Vigil, kept by Catholics, Anglicans, Lutherans and others, people gather outside, or at the back of a dark church, and a new fire is lit.

From it, one tall candle is lit, the Easter candle, and carried in slowly while someone sings: the light of Christ. People light small candles from it, then from each other, until the whole dark church is glowing.
In Orthodox churches, it happens near midnight. Every light goes out.

teach.h: CANDLE TO CANDLE, INTO THE STREET.
teach.b: The priest comes out holding a single flame and invites everyone to come and receive the light, and it passes from candle to candle through the crowd, out into the street.
John's Gospel has a line for it: "And the light shineth in darkness; and the darkness comprehended it not."

how: On Holy Saturday churches stay bare and quiet during the day; after dark churches in several traditions hold the Easter Vigil, lighting a new fire and the Easter candle and passing its flame from person to person, and Orthodox churches pass the light at midnight.

o: the quiet day of waiting between the cross and Easter
the Saturday Jesus rose again from the tomb
the day before Palm Sunday, when Holy Week begins

games.q: what's inside the day — tap the pairs.
p: Christ pulling Adam and Eve up

s: the Gospels describe Holy Saturday in detail
they say almost nothing: the women rested the sabbath day, and Matthew adds a guard at the sealed tomb.
at the Easter Vigil a new fire is lit in the dark
then the Easter candle, then everyone's small candles, one from another.
all Christians read he descended into hell the same way
some read a descent to the dead; others read it as a way of saying he truly died.

games.q: it's the Easter Vigil. the church is completely dark. you're holding an unlit candle, and a single flame is coming slowly down the aisle. what do you do?
o: light yours from your neighbor's, then pass it on.
wait until the lights come on.
games.why: the flame passes from one candle to the next until the whole church glows. one light becomes hundreds.

practice: Turn off the lights around you, or close your eyes, and let the dark be dark for a while, not knowing what comes next.
Near the end, turn on one small light, light a candle if it's safe, or simply open your eyes, and watch how much one flame changes a room.
If you pray, welcome it as a sign of what Christians wait for; if you don't, just notice the difference.

wordCard.voice: Holy Saturday. The quiet day between the cross and Easter, which ends in the dark with a new fire. Today's word.

orig.note: Latin: the light of Christ, sung as the Easter candle is carried into the dark church.

carryVoice: Your line: light in the dark. One flame, then a whole church. See you tomorrow.
